How does this occupation differ from automotive service technicians and electrical and electronics equipment installers and repairers?

This occupation mainly installs and repairs aftermarket in-vehicle electronics such as audio, navigation, communication, and security equipment, working within vehicle structures and interiors. Automotive service technicians mainly repair vehicle mechanical and powertrain assemblies; electrical and electronics equipment installers and repairers mainly work on equipment itself in industrial, transportation, and power settings.

How AI may change work for electronic equipment installers and repairers, motor vehicles

AI and digital tools can assist with consulting vehicle model information and wiring definitions, organizing fault codes and troubleshooting leads, and drafting repair records. They cannot replace actual vehicle measurements and harness checks, disassembly and routing work, fault root-cause judgments, or delivery conclusions confirmed with customers, and do not bear vehicle safety or warranty responsibility.

subject.name: Electronic equipment installers and repairers, motor vehicles
subject.summary: Following U.S. O*NET-SOC 49-2096.00, install, diagnose, and repair communication, audio, security, and navigation equipment on motor vehicles: check vehicle model configurations, perform disassembly/refitting, routing, wiring, and securing according to manufacturer information, commission and verify functions, and hand over vehicles under procedures while documenting warranty boundaries.
